title: EQT Group Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: EQT Persons
tiers.description: Directors, Key Management Personnel (KMP), all employees of the Company and its wholly or majority owned subsidiaries, and contractors and consultants who may come into possession of Inside Information. All substantive prohibitions (short-term trading, hedging, margin lending/encumbrance) apply to this tier without differentiation.

tiers.name: Non-executive director
tiers.description: Non-executive director of the Company or a subsidiary; distinguished only for Trading Request Procedure approval (Chair of the Company) and Director/KMP post-trade disclosure.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: Chair of the Company; distinguished only for Trading Request Procedure approval (Chair of the Company Board Audit Committee) and Director/KMP post-trade disclosure.

tiers.name: Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer
tiers.description: Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer; distinguished only for Trading Request Procedure approval (Chair of the Company) and Director/KMP post-trade disclosure.

tiers.name: Company Secretary
tiers.description: Company Secretary; distinguished only for Trading Request Procedure approval (Managing Director) and Director/KMP post-trade disclosure.

tiers.name: All other EQT Persons
tiers.description: Employees, contractors and consultants other than Directors and KMP; distinguished only for Trading Request Procedure approval (Company Secretary). Not subject to the Director/KMP two-business-day post-trade disclosure requirement.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the EQT Person in their trading with Securities, including the EQT Person's spouse, partner and children, the children of the EQT Person's partner, or dependants; and a company or any other entity which the EQT Person has an ability to control. Must seek clearance to trade through their EQT Person.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company's Board may specify any other Black-out Period in addition to the three scheduled periods. Confidentiality of such additional periods is not addressed. Separately, trading (including any exceptional-circumstances sale) is blocked at any time if the Securities are subject to a specific disposal restriction.

rules.detail: 'Securities' includes any instrument related to EQT Securities, such as options or rights that are tradeable, with no express venue limitation. Trading in Securities (including such instruments) requires prior written clearance under the Trading Request Procedure, must avoid Black-out Periods, must not involve Securities subject to a specific disposal restriction, and the person must hold no Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Securities means any type of securities in the Company (ASX:EQT) (including any instrument that is related to EQT Securities, i.e. such as options or rights that are tradeable).

rules.detail: Absolute ban on EQT Persons (and their Connected Persons) entering into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of holding Securities. No distinction is drawn between vested and unvested holdings, and no clearance or exceptional-circumstances carve-out is provided (unlike the sale-only exceptional circumstances relief available for Black-out Period trading).
rules.evidence: enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. 'Trade' is defined to include applying for, buying, selling or transferring any economic interest in the Securities, which would sweep in a prepaid forward or similar monetisation, subject to the ordinary Trading Request Procedure and Black-out Period restrictions; if the monetisation involves granting security over the shares it is instead absolutely banned under 14(c).
rules.evidence: Trade or Trading means to apply for, buy, sell or transfer any economic interest in the Securities, including electing to vary a Dividend Reinvestment Plan ("DRP") participation.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named or otherwise addressed anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.

CFDs are not named. They would likely fall within 'any instrument that is related to EQT Securities' and so require clearance as an ordinary Trade; a CFD that operates to limit the economic risk of holding Securities is instead caught by the absolute hedging ban in 14(b).
rules.evidence: Securities means any type of securities in the Company (ASX:EQT) (including any instrument that is related to EQT Securities, i.e. such as options or rights that are tradeable).

rules.detail: Absolute ban on EQT Persons (and their Connected Persons) entering into margin lending or any other arrangement where any form of security is granted over the Securities. No carve-out or clearance route is provided.
rules.evidence: enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Securities.

rules.detail: The ban is not limited to margin lending: any arrangement where any form of security (charge, lien, pledge) is granted over the Securities is prohibited outright.
rules.evidence: enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Securities.

rules.detail: The prohibition operates as a blanket ban on any secured financing arrangement against Securities, not just conventional margin loans, with no exemption authority.
rules.evidence: enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Securities.

rules.detail: Ban on short-term or speculative trading, i.e. trading in or out of Securities on market within 3 months of acquiring them, unless prior special dispensation is sought and granted in writing having regard to the Exceptional Circumstances matters in clause 19.
rules.evidence: engage in short-term or speculative trading in Securities i.e. trading in or out of the Securities on market within three (3) months of acquiring them, unless prior special dispensation has been sought and granted in writing.

exemption_authority: The relevant Approver (per the clause 9 table) may grant prior special dispensation for short-term trading within 3 months of acquisition, having regard to the Exceptional Circumstances matters in clause 19. Separately, an Approver may permit a sale (not a purchase) during a Black-out Period for severe financial hardship, a court order/undertaking or overriding legal/regulatory requirement, or other exceptional circumstances, provided the person holds no Inside Information, the Securities are not subject to a specific disposal restriction, and written justification accompanies the request. No exemption authority is provided for the absolute margin lending/encumbrance ban (14(c)) or the absolute hedging ban (14(b)).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any clearance to trade approval is required for a trade under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the trade would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a technically compliant collar clearance request can be refused on a subjective reputational/optics test, adding an unpredictable gate beyond the objective rules.

bespoke_clauses.topic: absolute margin lending and encumbrance ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: enter into margin lending or any other arrangements where any form of security is granted over the Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is barred outright with no exemption route analogous to the short-term trading dispensation or the Black-out Period sale-only relief.

bespoke_clauses.topic: absolute hedging ban regardless of vesting
bespoke_clauses.clause: enter into hedging or other financial arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike some peer policies, EQT draws no distinction between vested and unvested holdings: a collar (put plus call limiting economic risk) is banned outright at all times for all EQT Persons and Connected Persons, with no clearance or exceptional-circumstances route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance to trade may be withdrawn or refused by the Approver at their absolute discretion, without giving reasons. The decision is final and binding. If clearance to trade is refused by an Approver, this must be kept confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no appeal and no disclosure right if a collar-related clearance request is refused.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Securities are not subject to a specific disposal restriction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Incentive securities under a separate escrow or holding lock cannot be traded, hedged, or sold even via the hardship exception while that restriction remains in place.

bespoke_clauses.topic: connected persons must clear through the EQT Person
bespoke_clauses.clause: EQT Persons must ensure that their obligations under insider trading laws and this Policy are complied with by their Connected Persons. For the avoidance of doubt, a Connected Person must seek clearance to trade through their EQT Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a spouse or controlled entity does not escape the clearance, Black-out Period, hedging or margin lending restrictions.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy for any EQT Person or Connected Person. Clause 14(c) imposes an absolute, unconditional ban on margin lending or any other arrangement granting any form of security over Securities, with no clearance or exceptional-circumstances exemption available, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares is prohibited outright. Independently, clause 14(b) bans hedging or other financial arrangements that limit the economic risk of holding Securities, with no carve-out for vested or unrestricted holdings, so the put-and-call structure itself is also banned regardless of financing. Even an ordinary, unhedged Trade in Securities requires prior written clearance from a role-specific Approver, must avoid Black-out Periods and any specific disposal restriction, must pass the subjective 'Front Page Test', and the clearance (valid only 5 business days) may be withdrawn or refused without reasons. Because both legs of a funded collar are separately and absolutely prohibited with no exemption route, a bank should treat EQT as a hard block unless the company amends or waives clauses 14(b) and 14(c), which their drafting does not contemplate.
